comments: I've looked at this in every way I could think of, and got nothing more than 8x'small' kana and 7x2=14 unique non-repeated 'large' kana. The presence of a 'no' and 'wo' do sound like it should be a sentence with more sense, but I can't figure out anything. Using the kana<->romaji conversion code of the Kana keyboard (see CCZAS, CCX0001), all I got was 2784^VKJ45&_&*(_5&58%&74[=900 (with the _ being kana missing from the keyboard AFAIK). I tried converting the letters to number, simple alphabetic order, and ignoring caps to get the number keys. Assuming the pure numbers are actual numbers, the rest are to be kept as separate:
Nice 2885, with a 7 and two 8 (which is 16 and another 7), but I don't see much on the rest. [= got nothing, maybe it's supposed to be an operation? This seems to be excessive overthinking.

Therefore, as this may be genuinely no more than a visual gag, to do this sort-of literally it'd need way more vowels than English, but including e.g. German, French, Russian (especially) special accented letters would work. But I can't display those with this engine/font combo. Flatly transliterated it's boring and unfunny; so as a compromise, I fed it through Google Translate and edited it up. Yes, I machine translated Cross Channel.
BTW, GT has changed since I translated this line and it now returns something totally different and IMO not as funny. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source is deliberately garbled speech caused by the physical restraint. The English generates a long sequence of recognizable but unrelated words and proper nouns, giving the utterance semantic content the source does not have.
